as_told.title: Crick's spaceship seeding Earth with life

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says fungi have been found on the International Space Station, the crewed laboratory orbiting Earth, and links this to Francis Crick, the scientist who helped discover the double helix shape of DNA. In another episode, Michels says Crick believed DNA could not have formed on Earth in 100 million years, which led Crick, in his book Life Itself, to the idea that life was seeded here from elsewhere, and he mentions the astronomer Carl Sagan alongside him. Michels tells it because, if true, life on Earth may have come from space.
